newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Italian-style repast, French champagne for HK binge.
newsitem.headline: Italian-style repast, French champagne for HK binge.

text.p: Italian food and French wine will be menu highlights for a lavish Anglo-Chinese banquet to mark Hong Kong's handover next Monday.
Some 4,000 VIP guests will feast on a three-course Italian-style repast with champagne, serenaded by a string orchestra.

Guests, led by Britain's Prince Charles and China's President Jiang Zemin, will tuck into appetisers of smoked Scottish salmon and lobster medallions with lettuce on a filo pastry shell covered in a champagne and dill dressing.
This will be followed by stuffed chicken breast with forest mushrooms in a creamy herb sauce, white truffle risotto and baby vegetables as the main course.
Dessert will be red fruit pudding with raspberry sauce.

Vegetarians will not be left out, the South China Morning Post said. They will be served a vegetarian terrine with basil and tarragon mayonnaise, then cannelloni filled with spinach and forest mushrooms as the main course.
The repast will be washed down with Moet champagne or a range of French red and white wines.
Colonial Hong Kong's last supper marks the end of 156 years of British rule. China is taking back the territory but is allowing it to be a quasi autonomous capitalist region.
